narration.text: Here is the first rule to learn in this part of the lesson. Roads leading into a traffic circle have yield signs, and you must always yield to vehicles already in the circle. If you are slower than highway traffic, you must keep to the right lane whenever possible. Drivers in a funeral procession must use headlights and flashing hazard lights, and with lights on they may go through a red signal. An acceleration lane is for speeding up to join highway traffic, while a deceleration lane is for slowing down to leave it.

Here is the next rule to learn. Approaching a roundabout, slow down, keep right of the island, yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk, and wait at the yield line for a gap; with no traffic in it you need not wait. To exit, move right well before your exit, begin slowing in the deceleration lane, and slow to the exit ramp's posted limit. Other drivers, even on a green signal, must yield to a funeral procession until it has all passed unless they can go without crossing its path. A good question to ask yourself here is this one: Approaching a roundabout, which side of the island should you keep to?

Here is the next rule to learn. In a multi-lane circle stay in your lane, and once you pass the exit before yours, signal right and move to the outside lane. If you take the wrong exit, keep going off the ramp and find a way back; never stop and reverse anywhere on the highway. Slow moving vehicles include bicycles, horse-drawn vehicles and farm vehicles, and a slow-moving sign on the back warns they go twenty-five miles per hour or less. A good question to ask yourself here is this one: In a multi-lane circle, when do you move to the outside lane?

Here is the next rule to learn. You reach a highway by an entrance ramp, use the acceleration lane to match the speed of highway traffic, and must not cross the solid lines between the entrance and the highway. Stopping in moving highway lanes is not allowed; use the shoulder only for a breakdown or other emergency, turn on flashers and stay inside if you can. Near slow vehicles, adjust speed and position, pass only when safe, and use your emergency flashers while following one to warn drivers behind you. A good question to ask yourself here is this one: What is the acceleration lane for?
